title: Zuno OKF profile 1.0: experience-client document
description: Frontmatter of experience-clients/<name>/client.okf.md in a Zuno OKF profile 1.0 bundle: the upstream Open Knowledge Format 0.2 envelope (https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/open-knowledge-format/blob/main/SPEC.md) plus the namespaced `zuno` block. Frozen (zuno-demo ADR-0615): a change needs a new profile version.

okf_version.description: [OKF] Version of the upstream Open Knowledge Format this document follows (SPEC §12): always the quoted string "0.2". Repeated in every document so a reader can dispatch one file at a time (a declared deviation: upstream declares it once, in the bundle-root index.md).

type.description: [OKF] Document kind (SPEC §4): always "experience-client" in this schema.

resource.description: [OKF] Canonical URI of this document (SPEC §4): its file on the main branch of the repository that publishes it.

sources.description: [OKF] What the document was derived from (SPEC §5 provenance). Descriptive, never a grant: the tasks' declarations are the authorization surface.

generated.description: [OKF] How the content was produced (SPEC §5 trust): an actor (`human:<id>`, `process:<id>` or `<producer>/<version>`) and an instant.

verified.description: [OKF] Independent confirmations (SPEC §5 trust). Absent or empty: unverified; machine actors only: machine-confirmed; a `human:` actor: human-reviewed. Advisory, never a grant. Always a list (a declared deviation: upstream also tolerates a bare mapping).

status.description: [OKF] Lifecycle of the document (SPEC §5): absent means stable. For an agent it agrees with zuno.status: draft for placeholder, stable for active, deprecated for deprecated or retired.

stale_after.description: [OKF] Instant after which the content should be reviewed again (SPEC §5), with an offset.

zuno.description: [ZUNO EXT] What the mcp-gateway needs to entitle the logical agent name.

profile.description: [ZUNO] Version of the Zuno OKF profile this document follows: always the quoted string "1.0" (zuno-demo ADR-0615).

name.description: The logical agent name the client sends as X-Zuno-Agent. Matches the experience-clients/<name> directory and must not be the name of an agent.

tasks.description: Task names the client sends; each is tasks/<task>.md of the client, of which only allowed_tools is read.

classification.description: The data classification the client declares on its requests (descriptive; the client's deployment sets the X-Zuno-Data-Classification header). Its tasks should only allow tools whose min_classification it reaches.

access.description: Who may use the logical agent name.

groups.description: Keycloak `zuno` realm groups (JWT `groups` claim, without the leading slash) whose members may call the mcp-gateway under this name. Unlike an agent, an experience client serves every employee, so these are business groups (sales, consultant, ...), not an agent_* entitlement group; the tool policy still narrows each tool to its own allowed_groups.

maintainer.description: [ZUNO] Who maintains the bundle, shown by consumers.
